questions.question_text: For $x=2t+1,\ y=t-2$ with $0\le t\le2$, find the range of $x$.

questions.question_text: For $x=6-t^{2},\ y=t^{2}-4$, with real $t$, which restriction applies to $x$?

options.why: This reverses the inequality: subtracting the nonnegative value $t^{2}$ gives $x\le6$.
This excludes $x=6$, which occurs when $t=0$.
This applies the y restriction $y\ge-4$ to x instead.

questions.solution_text:
$t^{2}\ge0$
$x=6-t^{2}\le6$
Equality occurs when $t=0$, and every $x\le6$ is possible.
